surface.tagline: Sales at Avoca. Diver, hiker, and a people person from Vacaville.
surface.intro: I grew up in Vacaville, studied economics at UCSB, taught myself AI, and now I spend my days getting Avoca in front of the people it helps. Scroll down and I'll show you the rest.

river.heading: Where I come from
river.lede: Three stones in the river, before any of this made sense.

stones.title: The rock
stones.body: My mom tells this story. I was about three, in Vacaville. I stepped off a rock and fell, and it made me so mad I climbed back up and stepped off again. Then again. Not until I got it right once, but until I couldn't get it wrong. That's still how I work.

stones.title: The farm
stones.body: My older brother Colby runs a fish farm. I spent summers working with him, and it was the first business I ever saw up close. It's where I learned what a real work ethic looks like, and where I started getting ideas of my own.

stones.title: UCSB
stones.body: I studied economics at UC Santa Barbara. The plan was to join my brother after graduation. Right before my last summer I decided I wanted to go a different direction first, and that one decision set up everything that came after.

openWater.heading: How I decide
openWater.lede: I keep a ranked list of what matters. Every opportunity gets held up against it.
openWater.valuesIntro: I've written out my values in order. When something comes my way, I check it against the list before I check it against my bank account.

valuesTop.name: Relationships
valuesTop.line: People come first. I'm happiest doing things with other people, and I want to do right by them.

valuesTop.name: Freedom
valuesTop.line: To say what I want and do what I want, when I want. Financial freedom is part of that, not all of it.

openWater.moneyRule: Money matters. But every paying opportunity is quietly asking you to trade some of these away. I only take the ones that don't.

wallNote.quote: Retire by 30. True retirement is when you stop sacrificing today for tomorrow.
wallNote.caption: On my wall for the last year and a half.

stepBack.heading: Two months, solo
stepBack.body: The summer after college I backpacked through Taiwan, Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore and Indonesia on my own. It was a chance to step back and ask: do I like who I've become, and who do I want to be? I still do that audit on purpose. Where am I, where did I come from, where am I going, and does it all line up.

aiArc.heading: Then AI happened
aiArc.body: That was summer 2025. I came home and went deep: hours of videos a day, then testing what the models could actually do, building agents, automating the boring stuff. I started telling people about it, then doing it for them, and got a business license as an AI consultant. My mentors said get real industry experience. I look for good leaders, and I found them at Avoca.

islands.heading: The islands
islands.lede: Each one is a story. Follow the route, or pick an island.

deep.heading: What I'm doing now
deep.lede: The deep end. This is the work.

avoca.heading: Avoca
avoca.what: Avoca is the AI front office for home-service businesses. It answers the calls, texts and chats a busy shop would otherwise miss, and books the job straight into the CRM.
avoca.myRole: I'm on the sales development team in Santa Barbara. My job is to grow the company by getting it in front of the owners it was built for.
avoca.why: I chose Avoca for the people running it, and because the product solves a real problem better than anything I'd seen. It lined up with the list.
avoca.forOwners: If you run a home-service business and you've ever lost a job to a missed call, I'd like 20 minutes to show you what this does.
avoca.ctaSub: Pick a slot. No script, no pressure.

consulting.heading: Before Avoca: consulting
consulting.body: In 2025 I worked as an AI consultant. The biggest project was La Cumbre Country Club, where I presented to the whole team on bringing AI into the club and then completed a contract to do it. I also worked with small businesses, and the most useful thing I did was sit down with owners one-on-one and teach them.

project.heading: A project I keep tabs on
project.body: Fish farms lose a huge share of young fish early, and you can see trouble coming in how the fish behave. The idea: pattern recognition on video to catch disease, stress, hunger or low oxygen before it spreads. I started on it with my brother's farm in mind, and I still keep tabs on it.

items.quote: You have a real gift for communication, and it was clear how much thought and care you put into tailoring the conversation for us. … You made a real impact.
items.name: Adam Zubek
items.title: General Manager/COO, La Cumbre Country Club

items.quote: You spoke with real confidence and clarity, and the way you framed the information made it easy for everyone in the room to follow.

items.quote: That does not sound like a salesperson. That sounds like a friend.

floor.heading: The floor
floor.line: The long-term goal is simple to say: build a life nobody on the planet would trade me for. Ask me what that means.

about.title: About Roanin Podkin
about.description: Who Roanin Podkin is: Vacaville, a fish farm, UCSB economics, two months solo in Asia, teaching himself AI, consulting, and now sales at Avoca in Santa Barbara.

sections.heading: Where I started
paragraphs: I grew up in Vacaville, California. I was always looking for a way to make a few dollars, and my older brother Colby, who runs a fish farm, was the first entrepreneur I ever watched up close. I spent summers working with him. A few jobs along the way taught me what a real work ethic looks like, but I think most of it was there from the start.
I studied economics at UC Santa Barbara. The plan was to join my brother after graduation. Right before my last summer I decided to go a different direction first.

sections.heading: Stepping back
paragraphs: So I went to Asia alone for almost two months: Taiwan, Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore and Indonesia. I got my PADI certification on Ko Tao and spent four days on a boat from Lombok to Flores. Mostly it was a chance to step back and ask whether I liked who I'd become and who I wanted to be. I still do that audit on purpose.

sections.heading: Then AI happened
paragraphs: That was summer 2025. I came home and went deep: hours of videos a day, then testing what the models could actually do, building agents, automating the boring stuff. I started telling people about it, then doing it for them, and got a business license as an AI consultant. The biggest project was La Cumbre Country Club. The most useful thing I did was sit down with owners one-on-one and teach them.
My mentors said get real industry experience. I look for good leaders, and I found them at Avoca, where I joined the sales development team in Santa Barbara in July 2026.

sections.heading: How I decide
paragraphs: I keep my values written out in order. Relationships first. Then freedom. Then health, respect, confidence, bravery, resilience. Every paying opportunity is quietly asking you to trade some of these away, and I only take the ones that don't.
There's a note on my wall that says retire by 30. Underneath it: true retirement is when you stop sacrificing today for tomorrow.

sections.heading: Off the clock
paragraphs: Hikes, new countries, side quests, golf, pickup soccer, the gym, runs. Mostly, anything active with people I like. If you want to know what I mean by a life nobody would trade me for, ask.

now.title: What I'm doing now
now.description: Roanin Podkin's current work: sales development at Avoca, the AI front office for home-service businesses, from Santa Barbara.

sections.heading: Avoca
paragraphs: Avoca is the AI front office for home-service businesses. It answers the calls, texts and chats a busy shop would otherwise miss, and books the job straight into the CRM. I'm on the sales development team in Santa Barbara, and my job is to grow the company by getting it in front of the owners it was built for.

sections.heading: If you run a home-service business
paragraphs: If you've ever lost a job to a missed call, I'd like 20 minutes to show you what this does. No script. If it isn't a fit, I'll tell you.

sections.heading: What I'm learning
paragraphs: How owners actually buy. Hint: it's trust, not the cheaper install. I'm also still keeping tabs on an aquaculture project from my brother's farm days, and still looking for the next mountain.

contact.body: Two doors: email and LinkedIn. If you run a home-service business and want to see Avoca, you can book time with me directly.
